newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called off on weak technicals, weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called off on weak technicals, weather.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called lower Tuesday after a sell-off Monday broke key technical support levels, with forecasts of higher temperatures in the U.S. Northeast this week weighing on the oil complex overall.
"We broke trendlines, the weather is going to be warmer this week, and there are more gasoline imports coming over," said a trader, listing the factors pressuring oil prices down at the open.
Crude was called five to 10 cents lower a barrel. Heating oil and gasoline were called unchanged to 0.25 cent a gallon lower.
On Monday, February crude settled off 0.90 cent a barrel at $25.19. Feb heating oil ended off 2.45 cents a gallon at 69.70 cents and Feb gasoline finished off 2.27 cents a gallon at 68.09 cents.
Crude steepened losses after breaking key support of $26.00 and two trendlines, with one extending from the low of December 11 and the other extending from the low of December 24.
Dealers also noted heavy fund selling, with one large fund in particular rolling from February into March ahead of the Feb contract expiry next Tuesday.

The sell-off started in heating oil when regional weather forecasters called for temperatures to rise this week before another cold spell this weekend in the "heating oil belt" of the northeastern United States.
But, according to the extended forecast, meteorologists said Tuesday that temperatures in the Northeast will drop to much below normal for at least a week starting this weekend.

Dealers pegged support for spot crude at $25.00 and then at $24.74, which represents 50 percent retracement of Feb's move from the low December 11 of $22.73 to the contract high of $26.74 made January 9.
